source_text: 7 DE S0LE ET LUNA. De Sole et Luna, licet sint praesentanea nobis, Erratis; quod ego prius, putatis oranda. Sunt quidem in astris, sed non sua sponte currunt Omnipotens illos, cum conderet omnia primum, Locauitque ibidem cum stellis quarta dierum. Errorem antiquus quin cum *** Et quidem in legem iussit, ne quis illos adoret. Tot deos oratis, qui nihil de uita promittunt, Lex quorum in terra non est, nec ipsi praedicti Uos autem seducunt sacerdotes pauci <inanes> Numina qui dicunt aliquid morituro prodesse. Accedite legis <codicem> et di<s>cite uerum.
pass_a_gloss: Sol/Luna praesentia — non oranda. Non sponte currunt; Omnipotens collocauit. Lex: ne quis adoret. Sacerdotes inanes seducunt. Accedite legis librum — discite uerum.
pass_b_english: Concerning Sun and Moon: though they are present to us, you err; what I once thought, you think must be prayed to. They are among the stars, but they do not run by their own will. The Omnipotent, when he first founded all things, placed them there with the stars on the fourth of the days. ****** And indeed he ordered into law that no one adore them. You pray to so many gods who promise nothing about life, whose law is not on earth, nor are they themselves foretold. But a few empty priests seduce you, who say divinities somehow profit a man about to die. Approach the law’s book and learn the true.

choices.why: Accedite legis librum et discite uerum

choices.reject: lights run by their own will
